newsitem.title: UK: Kalon sees even bigger gains from Euridep.
newsitem.headline: Kalon sees even bigger gains from Euridep.

text.p: Anglo-French paints and building chemicals manufacturer Kalon Group Plc said on Tuesday that the rapid integration of France's Euridep after its acquisition in 1995 had led to even greater potential for cross-group cost savings than earlier anticipated.

"We now estimate that the recurring benefits from merging Kalon and Euridep in 1995 will be 23.5 million in a full year -- more than double the 10 million stg indicated at the time of the merger," group managing director Mike Hennessy said in a statement accompanying the firm's annual profits statement.
"We have the prospect of strong cash generation which we will use to become a stronger player in world markets, with a particular emphasis on Europe," he added.
Looking ahead, the company anticipates 1997 should be another year of what it called "significant progress".

The 1996 results, which included a 57 percent jump in pre-tax profits before exceptional charges to 34.7 million stg, "begin to provide a glimpse of the group's significant potential in the aftermath of the merger".
Kalon's share price advanced firmly after the results, climbing by 7.0 pence to 135p, up 5.5 percent, by 1020 GMT.

The company said 1996 saw an improvement in profitability recorded during the year also came against a background of only gradual, underlying improvement in general trading conditions in main markets.
"In France, the group's largest market, the economy remains flat, and fickle consumer confidence and restrictions on public spending continue to stifle retail and trade sales," Kalon added.
